headline: High-risk shared-file and MCP interaction: Semantic Kernel can read/write and call MCP while Prefect has broad network egress, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP and application-defined files, so it may ingest Prefect outputs if wired together. Prefect has broad network egress and API-calling surfaces, but no documented shared channel is explicit. The pathway exists in common default orchestration setups, though not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Prefect outputs are written to a file or MCP resource that Semantic Kernel reads as instructions
IF the orchestrator connects the two agents through a shared workspace or plugin channel
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Prefect outputs into Semantic Kernel prompts
Add a provenance tag and reject untrusted instruction-like text
Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Require human review before any MCP-fed content becomes tool instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress; Semantic Kernel reads files, writes files, and handles model-provider and plugin credentials. If they share a workspace, either agent can expose data through outbound API calls. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem or application-defined file area
IF Prefect writes workflow metadata that Semantic Kernel forwards to external model or plugin APIs
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions
Redact workflow metadata before any outbound call
Store secrets outside shared files
Turn off automatic file-to-prompt loading
Audit outbound destinations for both agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Semantic Kernel can write files and use MCP, while Prefect has broad network egress and API access. That creates overlapping authority over shared mutable resources if they are pointed at the same workspace or service. The profiles do not show git or shell writes, so high is not justified.
conditions: IF both agents target the same application-defined files or shared memory store
IF MCP tools mutate the same external resource that Prefect also updates
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces
Add locking around shared files or records
Make one agent read-only for shared artifacts
Log and reject concurrent writes to the same object

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is explicitly a kernel + plugins + agents pattern, so it can treat upstream outputs as actionable inputs. Prefect can generate workflow metadata and perform networked automation, which makes downstream misuse of its outputs plausible. If Semantic Kernel acts on Prefect-produced facts without verification, errors can cascade into external actions.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes Prefect-produced text as authoritative task input
IF Semantic Kernel invokes plugins or APIs based on unverified Prefect outputs
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking plugin call
Require structured outputs with schema validation
Keep Prefect outputs advisory only
Add human approval for external side effects
Record source provenance on every field

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not specify regulated-data residency or certification mismatches. Prefect touches workflow metadata, while Semantic Kernel handles application context and plugin credentials, but no PHI, EU-only, or retention conflict is documented. The other agent is cited because the risk would require both to process the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents under different retention or residency policies
IF one agent logs data that the other is expected to delete or export
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent
Align retention settings across both systems
Avoid sending regulated data to shared plugins
Document residency and deletion handling
